jobs.title: Drift Wood #14 · the mixtape
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 18, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, chin up, unkempt dark hair falling forward, sharp jaw; CHLOE — aged 18, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders. WOOD usually wears oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn even indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers. CHLOE wears alanis morrisette tee. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Chloe makes Wood a tape. Side A is instructions. Panel 1: a teenage girl sliding a cassette tape with a hand-lettered insert across a desk to a boy in an overcoat, school newsroom (in this panel: CHLOE, WOOD). Chloe says "Side A is things you should have heard by now. Side B is things you'll pretend you already knew.". Panel 2: close-up of a cassette case insert covered in tiny cramped handwritten capitals, a track list and a note at the bottom. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: a teenage boy holding a cassette tape reverently in both hands while a girl beside him looks unimpressed (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "This is a curatorial act. A statement. You've made me a—". Chloe says "It's a tape, Wood.". Panel 4: a teenage boy lying on his bed at night with headphones on, a tape deck playing, a closed drawing pad beside him, rain in the window, black and white, quiet (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized crab, seen from above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
